newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti sells stake in Omnitel to Mannesmann.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti sells stake in Omnitel to Mannesmann.

text.p: Italy's Olivetti group reached a deal with German engineering and telecoms company Mannesmann AG on Friday to sell a 5.8 percent stake in Italian mobile phone operator Omnitel Pronto Italia.
The deal means Olivetti's share in Omnitel Pronto Italia, Italy's second GSM cellular phone service operator, falls to 35.5 percent from 41.3 percent, an Olivetti spokesman said.

Omnitel Pronto Italia has two consortiums of shareholders, with Pronto Italia, of which Mannesmann forms a part, holding 30 percent and Olivetti-led Omnitel Sistemi Radiocellulari (OSR) holding 70 percent.
The transaction brings a much-needed injection of capital to loss-making Olivetti of around 300 billion lire ($200 million).

The struggling Italian group remains OSR's majority shareholder with 50.74 percent. But Mannesmann, which already held 5.9 percent of Omnitel Pronto Italia through Pronto Italia, has raised its stake to more than 11 percent and, now in both consortiums, it can appoint a representative to OSR's board.

Olivetti said the deal was subject to the pre-emptive rights of the other OSR shareholders, Bell Atlantic, Telia and CCIL, who had 30 days to exercise their rights on the same terms as those in the contract between Olivetti and Mannesmann.

Joachim Funk, chief executive officer of Mannesmann, said in a statement the agreement "significantly strengthened its partnership and will enable us to increase our contribution to the future growth of Omnitel. We consider Omnitel a great success story."
Olivetti CEO Roberto Colannino said: "The operation greatly enhances the value of Olivetti's investment in Omnitel."

Olivetti said 93 percent of the price, that is 404 billion lire ($266 million), would be cashed in by the end of 1996. The remaining seven percent would be paid half in 1997 and the other half in 2001 at the latest.
Olivetti also said it had sold some option rights it owned in Pronto Italia for 50 billion lire ($33 million).
Its share in mobile phone operator Omnitel is a key part of its strategy for the future, taking it away from the loss-making and fiercely competive personal computer business.

Omnitel Pronto Italia, which launched its GSM service in December 1995, reported a first half 1996 net loss of 260 billion lire ($171 million). The company expects to reach operating breakeven point in 1998. ($1=1521 Lire)
